intent: Write the per-series color custom properties of one ChartConfig into a style element scoped to a chart id, for a chart shell built without ChartContainer.
typical_uses: A chart shell of the caller's own that still reads series colors from a ChartConfig

instead.note: ChartContainer already renders ChartStyle for its own `data-chart` id, which it builds as `chart-<id>`; a second ChartStyle given the container's `id` targets no element, and one given the prefixed id only duplicates the container's rules.

invariants.text: The rules target `[data-chart='<id>']` with `id` reduced to letters, digits, `_` and `-`; they reach an element only when the caller puts the same reduced id on that element's `data-chart` attribute.
A `theme` entry's dark value applies under `[data-theme='dark']` and, when no `data-theme='light'` is set on the root, under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`; its light value applies otherwise.
An empty config renders no style element at all.

anti_patterns.dont: Pair ChartStyle with ChartTooltipContent or ChartLegendContent in a chart shell of the caller's own
anti_patterns.do_instead: Use ChartContainer when the chart needs the kit's tooltip or legend content; ChartStyle provides no config to them, and they throw without the one ChartContainer provides

config.states: config maps each series key to an optional label, icon component and a flat color or a light and dark color pair
config.because: `ChartConfig` is a record of objects whose `icon` is a React component and whose `color` and `theme` exclude each other, which the compiler emits no JSON type for.

good.title: Series colors for a chart shell of the caller's own

bad.title: An id the selector reduces but the attribute keeps
bad.why: The selector targets `usage_q1` while the attribute says `usage.q1`, so no series color reaches the chart.

config.description: Partially typed: ChartConfig.
